_comment: Human-authored input to scripts/build-skills.py, in the same spirit as
notes/synthesis/callout-classifications/*.tsv: judgement lives here, everything else is derived.
'owns' partitions the guide corpus' *reference guides*. Every part 1-17 must be claimed; a part
listed without 'references' owns all of that part's reference guides, and a part listed with
'references' owns only those, so the remaining ones must be claimed by another skill. The build
fails if that cover is not total and disjoint.
A part README is deliberately NOT disjoint. Part 16 is split across three skills, and each of
them bundles the whole part-16 README, because it is the shared router those skills' own
SKILL.md links into and each install is independent — a skill carrying 16.1 but no part-16
README would have dangling links. Keeping it whole also preserves the anchors that
SILENT-FAILURES entries address it by. What IS filtered per skill is everything derived: the
triage rows lifted into SKILL.md, the deep-guide list, the section maps, and both indexes.
'related' is a curated, deliberately directional list, not a symmetric graph. It answers 'where
would a reader of THIS skill go next', which is hub-and-spoke: a spoke names the hub it depends
on, while the hub names only the few skills worth surfacing to everyone. Making it symmetric
would give the broad skills a related list long enough to stop being a recommendation.
'description' is the portable triggering surface shared by Codex, Claude Code and the open
Agent Skills standard. Put both scope and when-to-use conditions there; name concrete symbols,
error strings and observed symptoms rather than topics. 'short_description' is OpenAI UI text,
and 'trigger_evals' contains portable positive and near-miss negative activation fixtures.
